title: Exterior cleaning methods that keep water and product out of the machine
referencesAtStart: Official references for this lesson: ACCC, Consumer rights and guarantees (business) (published and modified 17 July 2026, per page metadata).
moduleTitle: Shared: Job management and service delivery
audience: Workers who clean the exterior of commercial dishwashers, ovens, fryers, coffee machines, laundry machines and workshop machines
learningOutcomes: Select a low-moisture exterior method that suits the appliance's finish and controls
Keep water, steam and product away from vents, seals, connections, motors and labels
Clean stainless steel and painted surfaces without causing scratches, streaks or residue
Check the finished surface for residue, moisture and damage before handover

instruction.heading: Start dry, then use the least water that works
instruction.body: The method that protects an appliance is the one that removes the soil with the least water. Begin by removing loose debris with a dry cloth, a soft brush or a vacuum with a non-metal nozzle, and only then apply a damp cloth. Use a microfibre or other lint-free cloth dampened with the approved product, and wring it out until it is damp rather than wet. Work from the top of the appliance down, so that drips do not run over areas you have already cleaned. Keep the cloth moving and turn it often, so that the soil is lifted rather than smeared. Use a second clean damp cloth to remove product residue, and finish with a dry cloth. Avoid hosing, pressure washing and steam for exterior surfaces of most specialty appliances, because the water and heat can enter vents, seals, switches and electrical boxes, and they can drive grease into joints.

instruction.heading: Protecting the parts that water must not reach
instruction.body: Some parts of an appliance are sensitive to water even when they are on the outside. Control panels and membrane keypads can let water in at their edges, and water inside a control panel can cause a short. Vents and fan grilles draw water into motors. Door seals can be damaged by solvents or by heat from steam. Data plates and labels can lift or fade. Connections, sockets and electrical plugs must stay dry. Motor housings and bearings must not be wetted. Drip trays and drain outlets should be emptied and wiped, not flooded. Use the cloth only, keep spray off these parts, and wipe away from the control panel. Where the manufacturer's instructions name a part that must not be wetted, the instruction applies even if it is on the outside.

instruction.heading: Stainless steel, painted surfaces and glass
instruction.body: Stainless steel should be wiped along the grain using a clean damp cloth and a product suitable for stainless steel, then dried to prevent water marks. Do not use steel wool, abrasive pads or scouring powder, because they scratch the finish and make it easier for soil to stick. Painted and powder-coated surfaces should be cleaned with a mild product, because strong alkaline or solvent products can dull or lift the coating. Glass, including oven door glass, should be cleaned with a product approved for glass and a clean cloth, and never with a wet cloth on a very hot surface. Plastic parts should be cleaned with a mild product, and rubber seals with a product that the manufacturer or the SDS confirms is compatible. Test any product on a small hidden area first if the finish is unfamiliar, and record the test.

procedure: Confirm the surface is cool, the appliance is isolated, and the manufacturer's care instructions for the surfaces have been read.
Remove loose debris with a dry cloth, soft brush or vacuum with a non-metal nozzle.
Dampen a microfibre cloth with the approved product, wring it out, and wipe from the top down.
Keep water and product away from vents, fan grilles, seals, sockets, control panels, data plates and motor housings.
Wipe stainless steel along the grain, and use the mild product for painted surfaces and plastics.
Remove product residue with a second clean damp cloth, then dry the surface with a dry cloth.
Inspect the finished surface for streaks, residue, moisture at seams and any damage, and correct any issue before handover.
Record the method, the products used and any part that was excluded because the manufacturer's instructions forbade wetting it.

workedExamples.situation: A commercial dishwasher's fascia is covered with grease and dried detergent. The booking says the fascia should look new. The control panel is a membrane keypad at the top of the front, and the vents are on the rear.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How do you clean the fascia without wetting the control panel or vents?
workedExamples.reasoning: Remove the loose debris with a dry cloth. Dampen a microfibre cloth with the approved product and wipe the fascia from the top down, keeping the cloth away from the keypad edges and the vents. Use a second damp cloth to remove residue, then dry. Wipe the keypad with a dry or lightly damp cloth only, and do not spray it. Check the finish for streaks and record the method.

workedExamples.situation: A commercial oven's stainless steel door has a dull, streaked finish after the last clean. The customer asks you to use a scouring pad to bring back the shine.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you use the scouring pad?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not use a scouring pad on stainless steel, because it scratches the finish and can make the surface look worse over time. Clean with a stainless-approved product along the grain and a clean damp cloth, then dry. Explain to the customer that the finish is not designed for abrasive cleaning and that the surface is cleaned, not restored. Record the customer's request and your reply.

equipmentAndPpe: Microfibre cloths, dry and damp, colour-coded by task
Soft brush and vacuum with a non-metal nozzle for debris
Approved products for stainless steel, painted surfaces and glass, from the business list
Gloves and eye protection as set by the SDS and the business

commonErrors.error: Hosing or pressure washing the outside of an appliance to speed up the clean.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a damp cloth and a low-moisture method. Keep water and steam away from vents, seals and controls.

commonErrors.error: Using scouring pads or steel wool on stainless steel, leaving scratches that hold soil.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a soft cloth and a stainless-approved product, wiping along the grain.

commonErrors.error: Leaving product residue or a wet surface at the seams, which causes streaks and corrosion over time.
commonErrors.prevention: Rinse with a second damp cloth and dry the surface before handover.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Water near electrical parts is a shock and short-circuit hazard. The method in this lesson keeps water and product away from electrical parts.
The manufacturer's care instructions govern which parts may be wetted or cleaned with which product. Consumer guarantees apply alongside any warranty.

Cleaning of gas components and internal parts is excluded from this lesson. See “Gas appliances: recognising gas components and stopping work safely” and “Scope, authority and exclusions for appliance cleaning”.

qualityStandard: The surface is clean and dry, with no streaks, product residue or moisture at seams
No water or product has entered vents, sockets, control panels, seals or motor housings
No abrasive pad or steel wool was used on stainless steel or painted surfaces
documentationEvidence: The method used for each surface and the products used, from the business list
Any part excluded because the manufacturer's instructions forbade wetting it
The condition of the surface at handover, with a photograph where the business requires one
summary: Start dry, then use a damp cloth with the least water and an approved product.
Keep water and product away from vents, seals, controls, connections and motors.
Use soft cloths and wipe stainless steel along the grain. Dry the surface before handover.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the preferred first step when cleaning the outside of a commercial appliance?
options: Hose the appliance down to loosen the soil first, then wipe
Remove loose debris with a dry cloth, soft brush or vacuum
Apply steam to the entire surface before any dry work begins
Scrub the surface with a scouring pad to lift the soil

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part must water stay away from during an exterior clean?
options: The stainless steel top panel, which is most at risk
The floor under the appliance, which is already wet
The membrane control panel, vents and electrical connections
The outside of the rubber door seal, which is always dry

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should stainless steel not be cleaned with a scouring pad?
options: Because it makes the surface too shiny and not clean enough for the customer
Because it is always illegal to use abrasive pads on any commercial appliance
Because it leaves a blue colour on the surface, which is hard to remove later
Because it scratches the finish, which can hold soil and look worse over time

knowledgeChecks.question: How should stainless steel be wiped?
options: Along the grain, using a clean damp cloth and a stainless-approved product
In circles across the whole panel, so that the finish is buffed evenly
Only with dry paper towels, since wet cloths are hard to control on the surface
Across the grain at high pressure, so the cleaner can remove heavy soil quickly

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must you dry the surface and check for residue before handover?
options: So the customer can see the wet cloth that was used to clean the whole surface and check the drying
So streaks, residue and moisture at seams are removed, which protects the finish and the appliance
So the appliance can be switched on immediately after the handover, without any further checks
So the worker can avoid recording the method, and the handover is faster for the site contact
